errors.quote: A form is nondegenerate when its Gram matrix (the matrix of pairings of basis vectors) is invertible, which is why dimensions must be finite.
errors.problem: The causal link is reversed: nondegeneracy (trivial radical) makes sense in any dimension; it is the Gram-matrix criterion that needs finite dimension. The paper simply works with finite-dimensional spaces (F = Q^h or F_2^h, label space F^{\otimes 3} of dimension m) and never derives finiteness from the definition of nondegeneracy.

errors.quote: The basis vectors $\mathbf b\otimes\mathbf g_j$ of $A\otimes C$ span $B\otimes C$ and the vectors $\mathbf p\otimes\mathbf g_j$ span $P\otimes C$
errors.problem: Notation slip: $(\mathbf g_j)$ was introduced as a basis of $G$, but here it must be a basis of $C$; no basis of $C$ is introduced. The argument (giving $A\otimes C=(B\otimes C)\perp(P\otimes C)$, as in the paper's $A\otimes F=(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes F)$) is otherwise correct.

errors.quote: so a stage with no factors contributes a factor $1$.
errors.problem: Imprecise: no stage has no factors. In the paper the empty tensor product is used for $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$ at stage 1 (so $\dim A=1$, $P=A$ and hence $B=P^\perp=0$) and for $Q\subset F^{\otimes(3-j)}$ at stage 3. The page omits the consequence $B=0$ at stage 1 that the paper draws from this convention.
